# Reports That Run Themselves {#sec-parameters}



Much of what an organisation publishes is the same document with different numbers: the
monthly update for investors, one report per customer, region, team or model, a feedback sheet
for every class. Built by hand, each copy is a chance to paste last month's figure into this
month's file. Built from one source with a *parameter*, a value given at render time, each
copy is the same tested document run on a different value, and a script can make every one of
them and check it.

This chapter makes three: Acme's monthly investor update, a one-page report for each customer
segment, and, for teachers, a feedback sheet for each section of a course. The update carries
the company's business figures, which in this book are synthetic and labelled so on every
number; the model's figures beside them are the real evaluation's.

::: opener
- Explain what a parameter is, where its default lives, and how a value is passed at render
  time.
- Ask for a parameterised document that validates its value and chooses its value-dependent
  words by code, with guards.
- Render one document for every value with a script that names and checks each output.
- Say where the outputs of a parameterised document land in a website project, and why.

Start from
: your `acme-eval` repository at the end of @sec-white-papers, or
  `checkpoints/18-eval-whitepaper/`; for the educator's case, `examples/feedback/` without its
  `feedback.qmd`.

You build
: `update.qmd`, `segment.qmd` and a script that renders every month and segment; a feedback
  sheet for every section.

Checkpoint
: `checkpoints/19-eval-params/`, and `examples/feedback/`
:::

## One document, many values {#sec-params-vocab}

| Ask for | Quarto calls it | Check |
|---|---|---|
| a value set at render time, with a default | a cell tagged `parameters`, `#| tags: [parameters]` | the defaults render on their own |
| this value, now | `quarto render update.qmd -P month:2026-06` | the output shows that month |
| many values from a file | `--execute-params params.yml` | each value reaches the document |
| an output named by its value | `-M output-file:update-2026-06` | one file per value, none overwritten |
| the engine that injects the values | papermill, in the project's environment | without it the render stops |

: Parameters, and what each is called (Quarto 1.10.20, Jupyter engine). {#tbl-params-vocab}

The defaults are part of the document: the finished update's `month` defaults to
"latest", which it reads as the last month in its data, so its default
never goes stale; the segment report defaults to age\_band 60\+,
and the feedback sheet to section A. Passing `-P month:2026-06`
replaces a default for one render: Quarto adds a cell after the parameters cell that sets the
new value, and the document runs as before. That cell is executed through *papermill*, a
Python package the project must have: without it, a render with `-P` stops with "The
papermill package is required for processing --execute-params".

Two rules make a parameterised document safe. **Validate the value**: a month or a segment that
is not in the data should stop the render with a message that lists the valid ones, not
produce a report about nothing. **Let code choose every word that depends on the value**, from the
numbers as they are printed: "up" or "down", "above" or "below", "the first month in the data,
so no change". Chosen from the printed numbers, the word cannot disagree with them; guard what
code cannot choose, such as a typed caption, and check that the printed text agrees, as the
finished update does. A guard that repeats the comparison that chose the word can never fail,
and protects nothing. A document rendered for a dozen values is a dozen chances for a typed
word to be wrong.

## The investor update {#sec-params-update}

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Add papermill with `uv add papermill`, then create update.qmd, a monthly investor update parameterised by `month` (a cell tagged `parameters` whose default is "latest", meaning the last month in data/synthetic_business.csv): that month's business figures, each labelled synthetic, the release live that month and its real model metrics from outputs/, and the change from the month before with its wording chosen by code and guarded. Stop with a clear message if the month is not in the data. Formats html, docx and typst; render it for 2026-06 with `-P month:2026-06` and tell me where the files went.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
`uv add papermill` · writes `update.qmd` · `uv run quarto render update.qmd -P month:2026-06`
:::

Check it as an investor would, and as an auditor would. Every business figure says it is
synthetic, here; in your own update, every figure names its source. The model's figures come
from `outputs/` and are the real evaluation's. A month before the first release says so, rather
than inventing a model figure. And a month that is not in the data stops the render: try
`-P month:2027-01`.

::: pitfall
Where the files went is the trap. The project is a website, but the update is not in its
`render` list, and should not be: a site page shows one value, and an investor update is not a
public page. So Quarto renders it as a single file, beside its source, not in `_site/`, and
the site's post-render steps do not run for it. In the test run, `--output-dir reports` was
refused for such a file, and `--output` accepted a file name but not a folder, so the script
below moves each file into `reports/` itself.
:::

## One report per segment {#sec-params-segment}

The same pattern makes the per-customer, per-region or per-team report: one document, one
parameter per dimension.

::: {.prompt}
```default
Create segment.qmd: a one-page report for one customer segment, parameterised by `factor` (age_band or job) and `segment` (default 60+), with the best release's metrics for that segment from outputs/segments.csv against the whole list, wording guarded, and a note when the segment has few subscribers. Render it with `-P factor:job -P segment:student`.
```
:::

A segment's numbers deserve more caution than the whole list's: a segment with few subscribers
has wide, noisy rates. The finished report adds its note below 50 subscribers, a
named setting, `FEW_SUBSCRIBERS`, in the project's code; the right threshold is your call, and
belongs in a setting like that, not in a sentence.

## Every value, checked {#sec-params-all}

::: {.prompt}
```default
Write scripts/render_params.py: render update.qmd for every month in data/synthetic_business.csv and segment.qmd for every age band, in html, docx and typst, each file named by its value, into reports/; check that every file exists and contains its value; print a table.
```
:::

For the finished project that is ten months and
five age bands in three formats: 45 files, each
named by its value and each checked for it. The check is what makes a batch trustworthy: one
file that silently shows the default month, because a value was not passed, would otherwise
go out with the rest.

::: pitfall
From the test run: a PDF check for the age band "18-29" failed, because the PDF's text gave the
hyphen back as a soft hyphen; the finished script strips soft hyphens and treats every kind of
dash as a hyphen before it compares. And self-contained HTML, which carries its libraries
inside it, is far larger than the same report as a PDF; send the PDF, and keep the HTML for the
site.
:::

## The educator's case: a sheet per section {#sec-params-feedback}

The same method serves a teacher with several sections of one course: one feedback sheet per
section, comparing the section with the course, from one gradebook. The example's gradebook is
synthetic, generated with a fixed seed, three sections of students
identified only by number.

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Create feedback.qmd: one feedback sheet per section of data/gradebook.csv, parameterised by `section`, with that section's mean and spread for each assignment against the course, a chart with alt text, every sentence labelled synthetic and its wording guarded, and no student identifiers. Then write scripts/render_sections.py to render feedback-<section>.pdf for every section and check each one. Run it.
```
:::

Marks are personal data, so the sheet shows section totals only, never a student, and never a
group so small that a reader could work out who it is; the finished sheet stops if any group
it describes, each assignment's submissions included, has fewer than 5. With real marks, the rules of @sec-ai-policy and your institution's data
policy come first: build the document on a synthetic gradebook with the same columns, as this
one is, and render the real one yourself.

## Summary {.unnumbered}

::: keyideas
- A parameter is a value given at render time; its default lives in a cell tagged
  `parameters`, and `-P name:value` replaces it, through papermill.
- Validate every value, let code choose every word that depends on it from the numbers as
  printed, and guard what code cannot choose.
- Name every output by its value, and render and check them all with one script.
- A parameterised document left out of a site's render list renders beside its source; move
  its outputs where they belong.
- Label synthetic figures on every number, and keep personal data to group totals.
:::
